items.title: Square Factor Cadence
items.prompt: Determine the next number in this sequence based on the underlying progression.
items.hint: Consider the number of positive divisors for sequential integers.
items.explanation: The sequence counts the number of positive divisors for consecutive integers starting from 1: d(1)=1, d(2)=2... wait, for 1, 4, 9: d(1)=1, d(4)=3, d(6)=4. Rather, integers 1 through 6 have divisor counts: d(1)=1, d(2)=2, d(3)=2, d(4)=3, d(5)=2, d(6)=4.

items.title: Chameleon Camouflage Intent
items.prompt: Fact or Myth: Chameleons primarily change their skin color to blend in with their background surroundings.
items.hint: Think about how reptiles communicate and regulate internal conditions.
items.explanation: Chameleons alter their skin color mainly for thermoregulation and social communication, such as signaling aggression or territory, rather than active background camouflage.

items.title: Equilateral Wedge Balance
items.prompt: A regular hexagon is subdivided into six equal equilateral triangles. If three alternating triangles are colored dark teal and the remaining three are divided in half, what percentage of the hexagon's total area is dark teal?

svgDiagram.caption: Regular hexagon divided into alternating shaded sections

items.hint: Count the fraction of full equilateral triangles filled with teal.
items.explanation: Exactly three out of the six identical equilateral triangles forming the hexagon are shaded dark teal, which equals 3/6 or 50% of the total area.

items.title: The Cipher Key Assignment
items.prompt: Four cryptographers—Anya, Ben, Clara, and David—each safeguard exactly one unique security key: Amber, Cobalt, Jade, or Ruby. Determine who holds the Cobalt key based on these findings.
clues: 1. Neither Anya nor David holds the Jade key.
3. Ben does not hold the Amber key or the Cobalt key.
items.hint: Start by identifying who must hold the Jade key.
items.explanation: Since Clara holds Ruby, Ben cannot hold Amber or Cobalt, leaving Ben with Jade. Anya cannot hold Jade, so Anya and David hold Amber and Cobalt; with David excluded from Jade and Ben holding Jade, Anya holds Cobalt and David holds Amber.

items.title: Glandular Oddity
items.prompt: Which of these biological glands differs fundamentally from the other three in how it releases its secretions?
items.hint: Consider whether secretions enter ducts or travel directly into the bloodstream.
items.explanation: The salivary gland is an exocrine gland that secretes through specialized ducts, whereas the thyroid, pituitary, and adrenal are endocrine glands secreting hormones directly into the bloodstream.

items.title: Printed Epochs
items.prompt: Arrange these communication technologies in chronological order of their historical invention or introduction, from earliest to most recent.
items.hint: Woodblock printing originated centuries before European movable metal type.
items.explanation: Woodblock printing emerged first (circa 7th-8th century), followed by Gutenberg's movable type press (c. 1440), the rotary printing press (1843), and Samuel Morse's commercial telegraph rollout (1844).

items.title: Gear Teeth Match
items.prompt: If Gear A rotates clockwise, in which direction will Gear D rotate, and how many gears turn counter-clockwise in total?

svgDiagram.caption: A train of four interlocked gears in sequence

items.hint: Adjacent meshed gears always rotate in opposite directions.
items.explanation: Meshed gears alternate rotation directions: A is clockwise, B counter-clockwise, C clockwise, and D counter-clockwise. Thus, Gear D rotates counter-clockwise and exactly two gears turn counter-clockwise.

items.title: Grid Voltage Calibration
items.prompt: Select exactly 3 cells whose values sum to 50 to stabilize the circuit voltage.

gridPuzzle.instruction: Select exactly 3 cells that sum to 50.

items.hint: Look for a combination of two values in the teens and twenties that bridge to 50.
items.explanation: Selecting 11, 15, and 24 yields a sum of exactly 50 (11 + 15 + 24 = 50).

items.title: The Vanishing Footprint
items.prompt: The more you take from me, the more you leave behind. What am I?
items.hint: Think about walking along a sandy beach.
items.explanation: Every step you take leaves a footprint behind in your path.

items.title: Cosmic Distance Ladder
items.prompt: Arrange these celestial bodies in order of their average distance from Earth, from closest to farthest.
items.hint: Start with our own natural satellite and work your way out.
items.explanation: The Moon is closest (~384,400 km), followed by Mars (~225 million km average), the Sun (~150 million km at closest, though Mars's closest approach is nearer than the Sun), and finally Proxima Centauri (~4.24 light-years away).

items.title: Roman Century Steps
items.prompt: Determine the rule governing the sequence of Roman numerals and find the next entry.
items.hint: Convert each numeral to Arabic numbers and look for the growing increment.
items.explanation: The Roman numerals represent perfect squares: 1 (1²), 4 (2²), 9 (3²), and 16 (4²). The next square is 25 (5²), which is written as XXV.

items.title: The Great Wall Visibility
items.prompt: Fact or Myth: The Great Wall of China is easily visible to the naked human eye from low Earth orbit without any magnification.
items.hint: Consider the wall's width compared to human optical resolution from orbit.
items.explanation: Astronauts and NASA confirm the Great Wall is generally not visible to the unaided eye from orbit because it is narrow and blends with natural terrain.

items.title: Aviation Milestones
items.prompt: Arrange these historic aviation milestones in chronological order, from earliest to most recent.
orderItems: First supersonic flight by Chuck Yeager
Wright Brothers' first powered flight at Kitty Hawk
Maiden commercial flight of the Boeing 747
items.hint: Consider the transition from piston-driven flight to jet-powered travel.
items.explanation: The Wright brothers flew in 1903, Lindbergh crossed the Atlantic solo in 1927, Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier in 1947, and the Boeing 747 entered commercial service in 1970.

items.title: Alphanumeric Progression
items.prompt: Find the missing term that completes this alphanumeric pattern.
items.hint: Track the letter advancing forward and the number doubling.
items.explanation: Letters advance by consecutive increments (+1, +2, +3, +4) while numbers double each step (3, 6, 12, 24, 48). Moving 4 steps past G gives K, paired with 48.

items.title: Glass Fluidity Fallacy
items.prompt: Fact Check: Medieval stained glass windows are thicker at the bottom because glass is a slow-flowing liquid at room temperature.
items.hint: Think about how medieval artisans manufactured crown and cylinder glass.
items.explanation: Glass is an amorphous solid that does not flow noticeably at ambient temperatures. Medieval panes are uneven due to ancient manufacturing techniques, and builders simply placed the thicker edge at the base for structural stability.

items.title: Angle of the Golden Ratio
items.prompt: Examine the segmented circle diagram. What is the value of angle theta in degrees?

svgDiagram.caption: Segmented circle showing known angles and unknown angle theta

items.hint: The circle is divided into three sections; sum the known angles and subtract from 360 degrees.
items.explanation: A complete circle measures 360 degrees. Subtracting 150 degrees and 125 degrees leaves exactly 85 degrees for theta.

items.title: Quantum Reactor Cells
items.prompt: Select exactly 3 power cells that combine to reach a total output of 50 megawatts.

gridPuzzle.instruction: Select exactly 3 cells that sum to 50

items.hint: Look for two large double-digit numbers that leave an easy remainder.
items.explanation: Selecting 23, 19, and 8 gives 23 + 19 + 8 = 50 megawatts.

items.title: The Weightless Pocket
items.prompt: I can fill an entire room without occupying any physical space, and the more of me you take away, the darker things become. What am I?
items.hint: Switch me on when evening falls.
items.explanation: Light fills a room completely without displacing any physical mass or volume.

items.title: The Diplomatic Summit
items.prompt: Four ambassadors (A, B, C, D) sit in a row facing north. Deduce who sits in the third position from the left.
clues: 1. Ambassador D sits on one of the extreme ends.
2. Ambassador B sits exactly one seat to the right of Ambassador C.
3. Ambassador A is not sitting next to Ambassador C.
4. Ambassador D sits to the right of Ambassador A.
items.hint: Place D at the extreme end first, then position B and C.
items.explanation: D must sit on an extreme end; placing D at seat 4 allows B at seat 2 and C immediately to B's left at seat 1, leaving seat 3 for A.

items.title: Tectonic Outlier
items.prompt: Identify the geographical feature that does NOT belong with the others based on tectonic origin.
items.hint: Three are formed along divergent or convergent plate boundaries, while one sits over an intraplate hotspot.
items.explanation: The Hawaiian Islands were formed by an intraplate mantle plume hotspot, whereas the Marianas Trench, Himalayas, and Mid-Atlantic Ridge lie along active tectonic plate boundaries.

items.title: Metallic Misalignment
items.prompt: Which of these metals does NOT belong with the other three based on its state of matter at standard room temperature (20°C / 68°F)?
items.hint: Consider which element is famously a liquid under ambient conditions.
items.explanation: Mercury is the only metal among these that is naturally liquid at standard room temperature (melting point -38.8°C). Gallium, cesium, and francium have near-room melting points but remain solid at 20°C.

items.title: Subatomic Charge Balance
items.prompt: Select exactly 3 particle sensors whose recorded values sum to an electric charge of +15.

gridPuzzle.instruction: Select 3 cells that add up to 15

items.hint: Try combining two large positive readings with one small negative reading.
items.explanation: Selecting +11, +8, and -4 yields a total sum of +15 (11 + 8 - 4 = 15).

items.title: The Resilient Traveler
items.prompt: I can travel around the entire world while permanently staying stuck in a single corner. What am I?
items.hint: You affix me to send something through traditional mail.
items.explanation: A postage stamp stays fixed to the upper corner of an envelope as it journeys anywhere across the globe.

items.title: Server Rack Sleuth
items.prompt: Four distinct servers—Alpha, Beta, Gamma, and Delta—are mounted in racks 1 to 4 from top to bottom. Determine which server is in Rack 3.
clues: 1. Gamma occupies Rack 1 at the very top.
2. Beta is installed immediately below Delta.
3. Alpha is situated higher up than Beta.
items.hint: Place Gamma on top first, then find Beta's position relative to Delta.
items.explanation: Gamma is in Rack 1; Delta must be in Rack 3 and Beta in Rack 4 so Beta sits directly below Delta, leaving Alpha in Rack 2.

items.title: Fractional Decay
items.prompt: Identify the number that logically replaces the question mark in this mathematical sequence.
items.hint: Examine the divisor applied at each step.
items.explanation: Each term is divided by an incrementing integer: 120 / 2 = 60, 60 / 3 = 20, 20 / 4 = 5, and 5 / 5 = 1.

items.title: Cloud Weight Reality
items.prompt: A typical white cumulus cloud weighs as much as about 100 elephants (roughly 500,000 kg).
items.hint: Consider the vast volume of water droplets suspended in the air.
items.explanation: A typical cumulus cloud has a volume of around one cubic kilometer and contains approximately 500,000 kilograms of liquid water droplets.

items.title: Segment Counter
items.prompt: How many individual, non-overlapping unit triangles are shown inside the central geometric figure?

svgDiagram.caption: Regular hexagon subdivided into internal triangular units

items.hint: Count the smallest triangular sectors radiating from the center.
items.explanation: A regular hexagon divided by diagonals passing through its center forms exactly 6 non-overlapping equilateral unit triangles.

items.title: The Museum Shift
items.prompt: Four docents—Elena, Marcus, Priya, and David—each guard a different hall: Antiquities, Coins, Fossils, or Textiles. Who guards the Fossils?
clues: 1. Marcus and David guard neither Coins nor Textiles.
items.hint: Start by identifying Marcus's hall once Elena takes Antiquities.
items.explanation: With Elena at Antiquities, Marcus and David must split Coins and Fossils; because Marcus cannot guard Fossils, David must guard Fossils.

items.title: Elemental Oddity
items.prompt: Which of these chemical elements does not share a key physical trait with the other three at standard room temperature and pressure?
items.hint: Consider standard classification into metals and nonmetals.
items.explanation: Bromine is a nonmetal (halogen), whereas Mercury, Gallium, and Cesium are all metals.

items.title: Planetary Distance Ladder
items.prompt: Arrange these four Solar System bodies in increasing order of their average distance from the Sun (closest to farthest).
items.hint: Remember the asteroid belt lies between the inner rocky planets and the gas giants.
items.explanation: Venus orbits at ~0.72 AU, Mars at ~1.52 AU, the dwarf planet Ceres in the asteroid belt at ~2.77 AU, and Jupiter at ~5.20 AU.

items.title: Orbital Energy Sum
items.prompt: Select exactly 3 energy nodes on the grid so their combined values total exactly 50 gigajoules.

gridPuzzle.instruction: Select exactly 3 cells that add up to 50.

items.explanation: Selecting nodes 14 (index 1), 18 (index 4), and 18 (index 7) yields 14 + 18 + 18 = 50. No other 3-cell combination sums to 50.

items.title: The Silent Carrier
items.prompt: I have a spine, but no bones. I have leaves, but no branches. I can transport you across centuries without taking a single step. What am I?
items.explanation: A book features a binding spine and pages (traditionally called leaves), carrying readers through historic tales without moving anywhere.
